candidate.answerReason: Moving the upper triangular projection into the matching lower notch produces a rectangle three units wide and two units high, so the area is six square units.

methods.label: Move a triangle to fill the notch
methods.explanation:
The triangular piece sticking up at the top matches the triangular notch at the bottom. Each occupies half of a square between neighboring dots, with a horizontal side of length \(1\) and a vertical side of length \(1\).

Cut off the upper triangle and slide it straight down two units. Its three corners then fit exactly into the notch. Sliding a piece preserves its area, and the moved piece fills the notch without any gap or overlap.

The resulting figure is a rectangle. Counting the spaces between dots, its width is \(3\) units and its height is \(2\) units. Therefore the original polygon also has area
\[
3\times2=6\text{ square units}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Cutting and sliding a matching piece reduces the question to elementary rectangle area, without requiring a coordinate-area formula.
